title: A Unified Electrostatic-to-Spin Framework for Asymmetric Multi-Gate CMOS Quantum Devices
authors: Zeheng Wang, Yan Liu, Yue Hao, Genquan Han
abstract: In advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) quantum chips, compact gate stacks make it difficult to connect lithographic geometry, electrostatic confinement and many-electron spin filling in one transparent model. This connection is central to design-technology co-optimization (DTCO). Here we develop a reduced-order analytical framework for asymmetric multigate silicon quantum-dot devices. Its electrostatic core, the Poisson-kernel coupled-interface Green-function (PK-GF) model, agrees with an independent finite-volume solution at the millivolt scale for the matched two-dimensional problem, without fitting to that solution. We then pass the gate-derived confinement, rather than a harmonic or fitted potential, to a spin-valley many-body calculation for a jellybean quantum dot with N = 2-17 electrons at B = 5 T. The unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution supports occupation-dependent, Wigner-molecule-like charge localization but likely overestimates spin polarization. Complete active-space configuration interaction (CASCI) supports a low-spin branch within the tested active spaces, which aligns with the experiments. The workflow therefore connects CMOS layout, device electrostatics, and potential-determined quantum observables, providing an auditable modelling layer for CMOS-based qubit design and DTCO.
summary: The paper introduces an end-to-end analytical framework that models electron behavior in advanced CMOS quantum dots. It first solves the complex electrostatics using a novel PK-GF model, validating it against finite-volume methods. This potential then drives many-body calculations (UHF/CASCI) to predict spin and charge localization, providing a vital tool for designing solid-state qubits.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a unified model that connects lithographic CMOS geometry, device electrostatics, and many-electron spin filling in advanced quantum dot qubits.
main_result: The developed PK-GF framework successfully links the physical layout to quantum observables, showing CASCI supports low-spin states consistent with experimental expectations for qubit design.
method: The work combines a reduced-order analytical electrostatic model (PK-GF) validated against finite-volume solutions, which then feeds into advanced many-body calculations using UHF and CASCI methods.
model_or_system: The system is an asymmetric multi-gate silicon quantum dot ('jellybean' geometry) fabricated in a CMOS structure. The Hamiltonian is solved by first determining the gate-derived confinement potential via the PK-GF model, which then governs the spin-valley many-body physics.
key_observables: Electron occupancy, charge localization (Wigner-molecule-like), ground state spin ($S=0$), and the interaction-to-level-spacing ratio ($R$).
important_parameters: Gate voltages (millivolt scale), magnetic field ($B=5 	ext{ T}$), electron number ($N=2-17$).
main_assumptions: The PK-GF model assumes a coupled boundary system for charge redistribution; UHF is noted to likely overestimate spin polarization, and CASCI convergence requires careful active space selection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between electrostatic models (PK vs. PK-GF vs. FV) and show diagnostics like charge density lobes, correlation functions, and energy spectra comparing UHF predictions against correlated CASCI results.

This potential is then passed to the many-body physics calculation ($	ext{Potential} 	o 	ext{Quantum Observables}$) using UHF and CASCI, culminating in a full end-to-end workflow demonstration.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, auditable theoretical bridge connecting semiconductor device engineering (CMOS layout) directly to the quantum mechanical properties required for qubit operation, which is highly relevant for solid-state quantum computing architectures.
